one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is fiscal Q1 FY27 earnings, which by historical pattern (Oct 22-28 in prior years) should land in late October 2026 (date not yet announced as of 2026-10-02). Guidance was $4.1B +/- $0.1B revenue and $7.30 +/- $0.20 non-GAAP EPS; Seagate has beaten its own guide repeatedly, so a beat is likely, but the stock's reaction will hinge on management's answer to the 2026-10-02 Nikkei report that Toshiba will spend about 60 billion yen to double HDD capacity and aim for 30% share. I expect management to stress that nearline supply is allocated through calendar 2027 under long-term agreements, which could recover part of the 11% drop. The overhang of a credible new supplier, CEO 10b5-1 selling and a stretched multiple offset that. Net: median about flat ($835), spread a little wider than the 0.75/3.5 = 21% monthly vol (I used 22%) because earnings fall inside the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of 20x my FY28 (Jun-2028) non-GAAP EPS of $37 = $740 (60%) and a 3.5% FCF yield on FY28 FCF/share of about $28.8 = $822 (40%), giving about $775. Net debt is about $1.9B, which is immaterial against a market cap near $190B.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 non-GAAP EPS $37 x 20x forward multiple (what the market will look at in Oct 2027)

inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 guide of $7.30, then roughly 5-6% sequential growth (7.3/7.8/8.2/8.6) as HAMR density gains and contract pricing on allocated nearline supply build. Slower than FY26's 34% revenue growth.

About 15% growth on FY27. That is below the bull models' 22% revenue CAGR, because Toshiba's capacity doubling (targeting 30% share from about 10%) arrives in the FY27-28 window and limits pricing on uncommitted volume.

Seagate traded near 40x forward at the July peak, a level it had never held before; it is about 26x NTM today ($837/$32). Historically HDD makers trade at 10-15x. I use 20x as a partial de-rating once supply growth from Toshiba and possibly WDC is visible.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF about $6.5B / about 226M diluted shares = $28.8/share at a 3.5% yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Reported 232M, reduced modestly for buybacks ($283M in Q4) net of heavy equity compensation
About 80% conversion of FY28 net income (226M x $37 = $8.4B), less HAMR capex
Investment-grade (Fitch BBB-) cyclical hardware with peak-ish margins; a premium to the market's FCF yield is warranted while visibility lasts, but not the near-2.5% implied today

bear.story: The supply response arrives. Toshiba doubles capacity, WDC adds HAMR/ePMR output, hyperscalers pause digestion in 2027 and QLC SSD takes some cold tiers. Contract prices roll over for calendar 2028 and gross margin falls from about 53% toward the low 40s. EPS trends to about $28 and the multiple compresses to 15x, a classic cyclical peak de-rating; insider selling looks prescient.

base.story: EPS grows to about $32 in FY27 with FY28 visibility near $37. Toshiba's expansion caps pricing upside but long-term agreements protect calendar 2027. The multiple drifts down from about 26x to about 21x as the market prices a late-cycle.

bull.story: AI inference and data retention keep exabyte demand ahead of supply. HAMR (Mozaic 4+) ramps flawlessly, giving Seagate a cost and density lead that Toshiba cannot match quickly. EPS of $40+ for FY28 and the market sustains a 30x+ growth multiple.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $500 (roughly 15x my FY27 EPS, -40% from here) the market would be pricing an actual turn in nearline pricing or demand (contract renegotiations, a hyperscaler capex pause, or share loss on HAMR execution) rather than multiple volatility. For a stock with 75% realized vol, ordinary swings reach $600-650.

key_uncertainties: Whether Toshiba's doubled capacity, plus any WDC expansion, lands in 2027-28 and breaks the tight-supply pricing regime that drove margins from about 35% to 53%
Durability of hyperscaler AI capex and exabyte demand into 2028
QLC SSD substitution in nearline tiers if NAND prices normalize
What multiple the market will pay for a historically cyclical HDD maker once growth decelerates (it was 40x forward at the peak vs a 10-15x history)
HAMR yield and ramp execution versus competitors
reasoning: Facts: FY26 revenue was $12.2B (+34%), Q4 non-GAAP EPS $5.71, gross margin 52.7%, FCF $3.1B, 232M diluted shares, debt $3.6B vs cash $1.7B, and the Q1 FY27 guide is $7.30 EPS. The 2026-10-02 drop (about -11% to $837.52) came from a Nikkei report, picked up by Yahoo Finance, GuruFocus and others, that Toshiba will invest about 60 billion yen to double HDD capacity (Philippines-centred) and target 30% share from about 10%. WDC fell 7-13% the same day; there was no Seagate-specific news, release or filing. For a skeptic this is the right kind of risk: the bull thesis rests on supply scarcity, and a three-player oligopoly in which one player doubles capacity is the textbook start of a cycle turn. Other bear evidence: the CEO sold over $120M in 2026 and the CEO, CFO and CTO all sold into the rally with no insider buying (Form 4s, 144s through 2026-09-22); the multiple peaked near 40x forward; Fox Advisors downgraded in June; QLC SSD is a long-run substitute. Weighed honestly, the bear case is a 2028 problem more than a 2027 one. Nearline supply is allocated through calendar 2027 under LTAs, Toshiba's ~$380M is small next to industry capex and takes time, HAMR gives Seagate a density/cost edge, and the balance sheet is now investment grade (Fitch BBB-; Moody's Ba1; S&P BB+), so there is no credit or covenant risk. My fair value is about $775 (20x FY28 EPS of $37, blended with a 3.5% FCF yield), about 7% below spot. I set the 12-month distribution as lognormal with a median of about $790 and sigma of about 0.63 (below the 75% realized vol, since vol tends to revert but the cycle-turn risk keeps it high). I fattened the far-left tail slightly for a cyclical collapse, and the scenario mean is about $845. P(>= today) is about 46%. Research was limited: one consensus-estimate search was blocked, so FY27/28 EPS are my own build from guidance, and I could not open the original Nikkei article.
